title: Dell’Anna 2021 · Jazz duet contexts
citation: Dell’Anna et al. (2021). Does musical interaction in a jazz duet modulate peripersonal space?. Psychological Research, 85(5), 2107–2118.
notes: Published study settings are available for inspection. See the source-backed method and remaining execution requirements.

published_method.sound: 50 ms 784 Hz sinusoid, 50 Hz sinusoidal amplitude modulation, 5 ms attack and release. Near loudspeaker by the right arm and far loudspeaker near the partner chair, nominally 120 cm.
published_method.touch: DS7A, 200 µs constant-current pulse on right hand dorsum, individually set to twice perception threshold.
published_method.timing: Paired audio and touch nominally simultaneous. Interstimulus interval reported as 6000–8000 ms.
published_method.allocation: 60 trials per block with 12 each of A Near, A Far, T, TA Near and TA Far, with at most two consecutive trials of the same type.
published_method.response: Right-index response-box press for touch, omit for auditory-only catches. A separate tactile rating uses a 0–7 scale.
published_method.intervention: Two counterbalanced visits 2–3 weeks apart. Participants perform Autumn Leaves in E minor at 120 bpm with the same guitarist. Compare expected harmony with alternating semitone shifts. Both contexts have two performances, each followed by a tactile assessment. Location of the two trial blocks within these repeated assessments is unresolved.
published_method.analysis: Tactile-only normalized paired RT at near and far, with a raw-RT reanalysis.

stimulus_type.value: Stationary amplitude-modulated tone and transcutaneous electrical tactile stimulation

implementation_gaps: Requires a live musician, intervention and visit sequencing, fixed loudspeaker delivery and electrical tactile calibration.
The original modulated tone, ear-level calibration, exact timing and block-to-assessment assignment remain unavailable. The response flow also needs the speeded press and separate rating.
